trickyParts: The carry runs on every version write, so it reads the previous version only once the document has any approval at all (LatestApprovedReview), then parses the previous version and, when the approved version is not the previous one, that version too; both parse with pmdoc.ParseRendering (the renderer's own output), and a stored version outside today's schema is logged at WARN and carries nothing rather than failing the human's write.

The trigger reads the trees' server-owned ask attributes (state, answered_by, answered_at, copied_from), never the version's actor: the version an answer settles into may be credited to SettlementActor or share its window with an agent's edit; blocks carrying copied_from are ignored so a copy's document never carries on its source's answer.

CutDecisionBlocks keeps one empty paragraph in a container the cut empties (a blockquote or callout holding only ask blocks), since both parsers read an empty container as that and Render refuses an empty one; the browser's line-based cut need not be byte-identical to the server's, only agree on the fixtures' equalities.

An embedded Postgres 16 (zonky jar) with pgvector from the PGDG .deb ran the Postgres-backed Go suites in the pod, initdb'd with --locale-provider=icu --icu-locale=en-US so the rank collation test can tell migration 0049 apart; both dispatch packages' full suites take about 13 minutes sequentially and need -p 1 -timeout 40m.
deviations: The card's earlier-approval line and Show diff control sit under the question (the spec's placement), not between the document link and the question as the plan's section 2.5 implied; packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md records the one exception to 'nothing else separates the question from its options'.
